english.notes:
(i) See also offence wordings H2130 and H2234 - relating to intimidation of witnesses or jurors.
(ii) Giving false names to the police. This charge should not be used alongside other relatively serious criminal offences (such as theft, burglary etc.) unless there are significant aggravating features. More details of this Court of Appeal decision can be viewed in R v Sookoo 2002.
(iii) Although commonly known as 'attempting to pervert the course of justice', no such offence of 'attempting' exists at Common Law - see R v K J Williams (1991) 92 CrAppR 158. The above wording should be used for the common law offence.
(iv) A statutory attempt may only be the subject of a charge if it is the act which has the tendency to pervert the course of justice that is attempted.
